data.description:
Write the OpenAPI 3.1 document for the API and serve it from the binary. Spec: docs/SPEC.md §5.7 and §5.1–5.6.

Why: senior bar. It also gives the interviewer a precise contract to read, and the sync test keeps the handler's param allowlist and the document from drifting.

Scope:
- backend/openapi.yaml, OpenAPI 3.1: paths /healthz, /api/cities, /api/listings/search, /api/openapi.yaml. Components: Listing, ListingResult (with rank and relevance), PageMeta, ScoringMeta, SearchResponse, ErrorEnvelope, FieldError with the code enum from §5.5. Every query param with type, constraints, default and a one-line description; document the unknown-parameter rule and the page-past-end and empty-city behavior in the operation description. Examples lifted from §5.4 and §5.5.
- Embed with embed.FS and serve at GET /api/openapi.yaml with Content-Type application/yaml.
- Tests: handler returns 200 and the body parses as YAML; a sync test that reads the allowlist of param names from the search handler and asserts each appears under the search operation's parameters, and vice versa.
- Run one external validator once (for example `npx @redocly/cli lint backend/openapi.yaml`) and record its output in a task comment; do not add it to make check.

Acceptance:
- curl /api/openapi.yaml returns the document.
- Validator reports no errors.
- Sync test green; `make check` green.

Validation: the curl and the validator output, attached with --role validation.
data.title: OpenAPI 3.1 document, embedded and served at /api/openapi.yaml, with param sync test

Implementation done on feat/BC-6-openapi: c65c19e (doc + root embed package + one-line route), 9e25b1e (tests). make check exit 0. Go: httpapi 39 tests + 235 subtests, all packages 72 + 409, 0 failures.

Smoke on :18006: GET /api/openapi.yaml is 200 application/yaml with X-Request-Id and Content-Length 25817, the body is byte-identical to backend/openapi.yaml, HEAD works, POST is the 405 envelope with Allow: GET, HEAD. Server killed, no listener left.

Deviations: (1) READER SIZE. yamlsubset_test.go has 308 reader lines (about 245 not counting comments and blank lines) plus a 95-line TestYAMLSubsetReader. The plan estimated about 150 lines, with a fallback to a JSON-syntax document past about 200. I did NOT switch to the fallback: the brief requires readable YAML for the interviewer, and the plan's own Decision 2 rejects the JSON document as unreadable. Every feature the reader supports is used by the doc, and most of the length is the error paths (line number plus rule). Cross-checked once against js-yaml 4.1.0 in the scratchpad: 0 differences on the whole document. Needs a decision: keep it, or apply the fallback. (2) I dropped single-quoted scalars and quoted keys in '- key: value' items from the subset to shrink the reader. The doc uses neither, and both are now rejected with a named rule. (3) I added TestOpenAPIExamplesMatchHandler, which pins the examples the SPEC does not spell out (healthz ok and degraded, malformedQuery, InternalError) to the live handler output, so every example in the doc is tested.

Delegator verification @5c4b993 (merged master c2e5544+ after BC-5 landed; diff vs master = 7 BC-6 files, +1352): make check rc=0 (golangci-lint 0 issues; go test -race -count=1 481 passed in 7 pkgs, httpapi 274 incl. subtests; vitest 269/269). Implementer deviation accepted: the test-only YAML-subset reader is ~245 code lines, past the plan's ~200-line JSON-document fallback; kept because the plan's Decision 2 and the brief require a readable YAML contract, every accepted construct is used by the document, and the extra length is line-numbered error reporting. Reviewer may re-weigh. Subset narrowed (no single-quoted scalars) — the document uses none.

backend/openapi.yaml: validated in 56ms

Woohoo! Your API description is valid.
You have 4 warnings.


Justification for each warning (0 errors; 4 warnings, all accepted per plan Decision 4 and Resolutions 5, 6 and 8; no redocly config file is added):
1. info-license (#/info): deliberately no license claim. The repo has no LICENSE file, and asserting one (for example LicenseRef-Proprietary) is a legal claim the author is not placed to make (plan Resolution 6).
2. operation-4xx-response on GET /healthz: the operation has no client-error response (it is a liveness/readiness check with no parameters). A `default` response does not satisfy the rule, and documenting 405 under `get` would be untrue, since a 405 is never the response to a GET (plan Decision 4).
3. operation-4xx-response on GET /api/cities: no client-error response; query parameters are ignored there (the unknown-parameter rule applies to search only). A `default` response does not satisfy the rule, and a 405 under `get` would be untrue (plan Decision 4).
4. operation-4xx-response on GET /api/openapi.yaml: no client-error response; it returns the embedded document byte for byte. A `default` response does not satisfy the rule, and a 405 under `get` would be untrue (plan Decision 4).

BC-6 complete at in_validation, handed to the Orchestrator (HEAD 70518b5, master bf36a3d merged in). The route is one line in NewRouter (application/yaml, Content-Length). Tests: served bytes == file; parses under a strict stdlib-only YAML-subset reader (test-only); paths == router; params == httpapi.SearchQueryParams() both directions plus order; examples == SPEC/handlers; code enums; 405 row. Deviations: the reader is ~245 code lines vs the plan's ~200 fallback (kept; upheld by both reviewers); the subset was narrowed (no single-quoted scalars); info.license omitted (4 justified lint warnings).
